paragraphs: Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yirmeyah were Rabbi Zeaira’s students; some say Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Zeaira were Rabbi Yochanan’s students: Bekhorot 30a, end. Rabbi Yirmeyah and Rabbi Yonah in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: HaZahav 57a and Temurah 27b. Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose—it appears it should read Yesei, who is Rav Assi—went before an official in Antioch. He rose before them, saying he had seen their likenesses in battle and prevailed: Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, Ein Omdin, mishnah 1. He heard that Rabbi Yose’s son had died. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Megalchin, halakhah 7: Rabbi Abbahu’s son. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 34a, quotes Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s son; this is certainly a scribal error. He fasted all day, although he had already eaten: Jerusalem Talmud, Nedarim 8:1; there, beginning of HaNoder Min HaYerek, with Rabbi Yose. He expounded at the entrance to the Nasi’s house: Mi SheHechshikh 155b. In Chullin 43b: ‘Yonah said: Rabbi Zeira said, the swallowing place.’ Rabbenu Yerucham explains that Yonah is a sage’s name. Likewise HaNizakin 59a, Berakhot, chapter 2, 14a, Avodah Zarah 14a, Megillah 16: ‘Rabbi Yonah said: Rabbi Zeira said.’ See Torat Chayim and Chokhmat Shlomo, against some interpreters’ view. Shabbat 10a: Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Zeira, one said this and one said that. In Challah, chapter 3, Rabbi Zeaira leaned upon Rabbi Yonah. Sedeh Yehoshua explains that Rabbi Yonah was his student, as Challah, chapter 1, has Rabbi Yonah speaking in Rabbi Zeaira’s name.
